title: Whose washing is it?
setting: Saturday, late morning, at the flat Kenta shares with Sora. Yuki has come round so they can go to a movie together, but Kenta is still in the middle of the housework.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: ケンタ、来たよ。もう行ける？
lines.kana: けんた、きたよ。もういける？
lines.english: Kenta, I'm here. Ready to go?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen, mada. asa kara zutto kaji shiteru n da. sora, kyou shigoto da kara.
lines.ja: ごめん、まだ。朝からずっと家事してるんだ。ソラ、今日仕事だから。
lines.kana: ごめん、まだ。あさからずっとかじしてるんだ。そら、きょうしごとだから。
lines.english: Sorry, not yet. I've been doing housework all morning. Sora's at work today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka, taihen da ne. jaa, tetsudau yo. ato nani yaru no?
lines.ja: そっか、大変だね。じゃあ、手伝うよ。あと何やるの？
lines.kana: そっか、たいへんだね。じゃあ、てつだうよ。あとなにやるの？
lines.english: Oh, that's a lot. I'll help, then. What's left?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: honto? sentakumono wa mou hoshita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.
lines.ja: ほんと？洗濯物はもう干したから、あとは掃除機かけるだけ。
lines.kana: ほんと？せんたくものはもうほしたから、あとはそうじきかけるだけ。
lines.english: Really? I've already hung the washing out, so it's just the vacuuming now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa tenki ii kara, sentakumono sugu kawaku yo.
lines.ja: 今日は天気いいから、洗濯物すぐ乾くよ。
lines.kana: きょうはてんきいいから、せんたくものすぐかわくよ。
lines.english: The weather's nice today, so the washing will dry in no time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. jaa, soujiki kakechau ne. ato de, fuku tatamu no tetsudatte.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、掃除機かけちゃうね。あとで、服畳むの手伝って。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、そうじきかけちゃうね。あとで、ふくたたむのてつだって。
lines.english: Yeah. Right, I'll get the vacuuming done. Help me fold the clothes after, okay?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? kyuu ni ame futte kita! kenta!
lines.ja: あれ？急に雨降ってきた！ケンタ！
lines.kana: あれ？きゅうにあめふってきた！けんた！
lines.english: Huh? It's suddenly started raining! Kenta!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: soujiki tomete! ame da yo! sentakumono, hayaku naka ni irenakya!
lines.ja: 掃除機止めて！雨だよ！洗濯物、早く中に入れなきゃ！
lines.kana: そうじきとめて！あめだよ！せんたくもの、はやくなかにいれなきゃ！
lines.english: Turn the vacuum off! It's raining! We need to get the washing in, quick!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yokatta, maniatta. demo sentakumono, mada kawaitenai no mo aru na.
lines.ja: よかった、間に合った。でも洗濯物、まだ乾いてないのもあるな。
lines.kana: よかった、まにあった。でもせんたくもの、まだかわいてないのもあるな。
lines.english: Phew, we made it. But some of the washing still isn't dry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, kawaitenai sentakumono wa heya ni hoshite. watashi wa fuku tatamu ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、乾いてない洗濯物は部屋に干して。私は服畳むね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、かわいてないせんたくものはへやにほして。わたしはふくたたむね。
lines.english: Then hang the damp washing up indoors. I'll fold the clothes.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou. a, sora no fuku wa tatamanakute ii yo. douse heya chirakatteru shi.
lines.ja: ありがとう。あ、ソラの服は畳まなくていいよ。どうせ部屋散らかってるし。
lines.kana: ありがとう。あ、そらのふくはたたまなくていいよ。どうせへやちらかってるし。
lines.english: Thanks. Oh, don't bother folding Sora's clothes. His room's a mess anyway.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sora no fuku? nee, kore, zenbu kenta no ja nai?
lines.ja: ソラの服？ねえ、これ、全部ケンタのじゃない？
lines.kana: そらのふく？ねえ、これ、ぜんぶけんたのじゃない？
lines.english: Sora's clothes? Hey, aren't these all yours?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? a, honto da. sou ieba sora, jibun no wa jibun de aratteru n datta.
lines.ja: え？あ、ほんとだ。そういえばソラ、自分のは自分で洗ってるんだった。
lines.kana: え？あ、ほんとだ。そういえばそら、じぶんのはじぶんであらってるんだった。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, you're right. Come to think of it, Sora washes his own stuff himself.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nan da. sora mo chanto kaji shiteru jan.
lines.ja: なんだ。ソラもちゃんと家事してるじゃん。
lines.kana: なんだ。そらもちゃんとかじしてるじゃん。
lines.english: Well then. So Sora does do his share of the housework.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou da na. zenbu hitori de kaji shiteru to omotteta.
lines.ja: そうだな。全部一人で家事してると思ってた。
lines.kana: そうだな。ぜんぶひとりでかじしてるとおもってた。
lines.english: Yeah, fair enough. I thought I was doing all the housework on my own.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hora, hayaku soujiki kakete. eiga, hajimatchau yo.
lines.ja: ほら、早く掃除機かけて。映画、始まっちゃうよ。
lines.kana: ほら、はやくそうじきかけて。えいが、はじまっちゃうよ。
lines.english: Come on, hurry up and vacuum. The movie's going to start without us.

choices.english: The rain soaks the washing before they can get it in, so they call off the movie.
Yuki folds Sora's clothes for him, and Kenta says Sora never does any housework.
Kenta thought he was doing all the housework, but the washing is all his own: Sora washes his own clothes.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenta says he's been doing housework all morning because Sora is at work. Line 12: he tells Yuki not to bother folding Sora's clothes, but in line 13 she points out that everything is his (zenbu kenta no ja nai?). Line 14: he remembers that Sora washes his own clothes himself, and in lines 15-16 Yuki teases him and he admits he thought he was doing all the housework alone. A is wrong: the rain does start (line 7), but they get the washing in in time (line 10: yokatta, maniatta), and in line 17 Yuki is still hurrying him so they don't miss the movie. B is wrong: there are no clothes of Sora's to fold (line 13), and the scene ends with Kenta finding out that Sora does do his own share (lines 14-16).

questions.english: On Monday, Mai asks you about your weekend: "shuumatsu, nani shiteta no?" Say you spent it doing housework.
questions.kana: しゅうまつ、なにしてたの？
questions.answer: Say you were doing the housework: kaji (o) suru, in the -teta form for 'was doing' (kaji shiteta). You can add when or how long: doyoubi wa (on Saturday), ichinichi (all day), zutto uchi de (at home the whole time).

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi wa ichinichi kaji shiteta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日は一日家事してたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I spent all of Saturday doing housework.

modelAnswers.romaji: zutto uchi de kaji shiteta. tsukareta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ずっとうちで家事してた。疲れたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I was home doing housework the whole time. I'm worn out.

questions.explanation: Lines 2, 15 and 16: kaji covers all the housework (cooking, cleaning, laundry), and it takes suru, like souji or sentaku. Kenta says asa kara zutto kaji shiteru (I've been doing housework all morning), and later admits he thought he was doing it all alone (hitori de kaji shiteru to omotteta). Don't translate 'housework' word for word as uchi no shigoto: say kaji. Mai is a friend asking casually, so drop o (kaji shiteta); kaji yatteta is just as natural.

questions.english: Yuki asks what's left to do, and Kenta tells her about the washing. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは洗濯物について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはせんたくものについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa sentakumono ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I've already hung the washing up on hangers, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou kaketa kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

choices.english: I've already hung the washing out to dry, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou hoshita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

choices.english: The washing's already dry, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou kawaita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenta says sentakumono wa mou hoshita: hosu is putting the washing out to dry, and he had done that already. A is English 'hang' carried over: kakeru hangs a coat on a hook or a shirt on a hanger, but washing put out to dry is always hosu. C swaps in the partner verb: kawaku is the washing drying by itself, and it wasn't dry yet. In line 5 Yuki says it will dry soon (sugu kawaku yo), and in line 10 some of it still isn't (mada kawaitenai).

questions.english: After they rush the washing inside, Kenta says, "demo sentakumono, mada kawaitenai no mo aru na." What's the problem?
questions.ja: 洗濯物は、どうでしたか？
questions.kana: せんたくものは、どうでしたか？

choices.english: Some of it still wasn't dry.
Some of it had got soaked in the rain.
Some of it hadn't been hung out yet.

questions.explanation: Line 10: kawaitenai is kawaku (the washing drying by itself) in the negative -teru form, and mada makes it 'still not dry'. Yuki had expected it to dry quickly in the sun (line 5: sugu kawaku yo), but the sudden rain brought it in early, so in line 11 she says to hang the damp things up indoors. B is wrong: Kenta's yokatta, maniatta (phew, we made it) means they got it in before the rain reached it; still damp from the wash is not the same as soaked by rain. C mixes kawaku up with hosu: hanging it out is hosu, and Kenta had done that already (line 4: mou hoshita).

questions.english: Kenta has brought in the dry washing and asks, "sentakumono, zenbu kawaita yo. chotto tetsudatte kureru?" Say you'll fold the clothes.
questions.ja: 洗濯物、全部乾いたよ。ちょっと手伝ってくれる？
questions.kana: せんたくもの、ぜんぶかわいたよ。ちょっとてつだってくれる？
questions.romaji: sentakumono, zenbu kawaita yo. chotto tetsudatte kureru?
questions.answer: Offer to fold the clothes: fuku (o) tatamu. Casually, watashi ga fuku tatamu ne (I'll fold the clothes), or fuku tatamu no tetsudau yo (I'll help fold them).

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. jaa, watashi ga fuku tatamu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。じゃあ、私が服畳むね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I'll fold the clothes, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, fuku tatamu no tetsudau yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、服畳むの手伝うよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll help fold the clothes.

questions.explanation: Lines 6, 11 and 12: folding clothes is tatamu. Kenta asks for help with it (fuku tatamu no tetsudatte), Yuki takes it on (watashi wa fuku tatamu ne), and Kenta says she needn't fold Sora's (tatamanakute ii yo). Don't use oru for 'fold' here: oru is folding paper, as in origami, or snapping something (hone o oru, break a bone), so fuku o oru sounds wrong. Futons and umbrellas are tatamu too. Kenta is a friend, so drop o and keep it casual.

questions.english: Kenta says, "ato de minna kuru n da kedo, heya, chotto kirei ni shitoite kureru?" Offer to vacuum.
questions.ja: あとでみんな来るんだけど、部屋、ちょっときれいにしといてくれる？
questions.kana: あとでみんなくるんだけど、へや、ちょっときれいにしといてくれる？
questions.romaji: ato de minna kuru n da kedo, heya, chotto kirei ni shitoite kureru?
questions.answer: Offer to run the vacuum: soujiki (o) kakeru. The -toku form fits, since people are coming and you're doing it ahead: soujiki kaketoku ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. jaa, soujiki kaketoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。じゃあ、掃除機かけとくね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I'll run the vacuum round before they get here.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、今掃除機かけるよ。

questions.explanation: Lines 4, 6 and 17: Kenta still has to vacuum (soujiki kakeru dake), says he'll get it done (soujiki kakechau ne), and Yuki hurries him at the end (hayaku soujiki kakete). English 'vacuum' is a verb, but Japanese has no verb for it: you run the machine with kakeru, the same kakeru as mezamashi o kakeru (set an alarm). Casual soujiki suru is also heard; souji suru is cleaning in general, and soujiki o tsukau (use the vacuum) is correct but not how people usually say it. The -toku in kaketoku means doing it ahead, before everyone arrives.
